newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Chinese, U.S. ministers discuss October summit.
newsitem.headline: Chinese, U.S. ministers discuss October summit.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen met for the second time in two days on Sunday to discuss issues related to a Sino-American summit set for October, officials said.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Albright had asked Qian for the unscheduled meeting in order to "go over some more summit items". He did not specify the issues.

Albright "wanted to explain our thinking behind why we were proposing some of these initiatives and in a couple of cases she wanted to cut through some of the problems in reaching an agreement on others", he told reporters.

The two ministers had met for two hours on Saturday to plan the summit, which officials have tentatively scheduled for October 28. They are in Malaysia for the annual meeting of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
During a news conference before his talks with Albright on Saturday, Qian said the summit should be substantive not just show, raising expectations it would produce concrete results.

The United States has insisted the summit between President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin make real progress on key issues. But that was the first time a high- ranking Chinese official had publicly expressed a similar view.
Planning for the summit is intensifying, with three bilateral teams focusing on trade, nonproliferation and strategic issues.
